4f3bbe985dbc1ac2dce481360b759afb5a50f09d: Borno is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 13 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. The terrain is serious at Borno, with 24 black runs and 72 red runs on offer, so confirmed skiers will find plenty to challenge them. Off-piste and freeride are practised here, often in excellent conditions thanks to the altitude and the exposure of the slopes. Borno's modest altitude, from 956 m at the village to 1694 m at the summit, makes it sensitive to changes in the weather. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. At 37€, the day lift pass places Borno among the intermediate resorts on budget: neither cheap nor extortionate. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies the price for most skiers. In short, Borno does not compete with the giants of skiing, and does not claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

4fb386a3de5d1c7f5c97bf51c850e5d178d28ba9: A resort on a human scale, Bosco Gurin focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 30 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly renew their playground. Bosco Gurin has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoiled landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands in contrast to the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Bosco Gurin's altitude (1482 m at the base, 2331 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Bosco Gurin is clearly high: 60€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you need to be aware of it before you go. In short, Bosco Gurin does not compete with the giants of skiing, and does not claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
